U04_nixpkgs_hello_drvPath.headline: CORRECTED 2026-07-22: byte-identical, YES. But sui is ~7x SLOWER than nix in load-robust user-CPU (2.15s vs 0.30s) — the prior '1.4x FASTER' was a wall-time artifact. See user_cpu_load_robust. The wall win was not real; the CPU gap is the honest stratosphere target.

user_cpu_load_robust.metric: user-CPU seconds (/usr/bin/time -p), the LOAD-ROBUST metric — wall is contaminated by machine load (measured: this expr read 10-26s wall under a 16-agent workflow while user-CPU held ~2.1s)
user_cpu_load_robust.note: Apples-to-apples in real CPU. nix's eval of hello.drvPath is ~0.30s CPU cold OR warm (the eval-cache barely helps — it is just cheap). BOTH sui engines are ~2.15s (the VM accelerator is NOT faster here — the cost is the SHARED substrate: rowan AST re-walk + im_rc HAMT env COW-per-bind, per the dhat top_churn).
user_cpu_load_robust.honest_finding: sui is ~7x SLOWER than nix in real CPU on the classic leaf. The `sui_plain_wall_s: 1.54 / ~1.4x FASTER` headline below was MISLEADING — it compared WALL time, where nix's 2.2s wall is mostly non-CPU overhead (its real eval work is 0.30s CPU) and sui's 1.54s wall is multithreaded compute doing 2.15s of CPU work. Never round up: in computational efficiency sui trails nix ~7x here.
user_cpu_load_robust.target_lever: L3 IR (eval_ir / STRATOSPHERE M5) — lower-once flat IR eliminates the rowan re-walk (40.7% heap / 21% wall self-time per the profile), the shared cost both engines pay. That, plus the im_rc env-COW work, is the quantified path from 2.15s toward nix's 0.30s.

perf_ratchet_protocol.rule: The perf ratchet keys on LOAD-ROBUST user-CPU (/usr/bin/time user), never wall-time. Wall-time under uncontrolled machine load produces FALSE regressions (measured: hello.drvPath 10-26s wall under a 16-agent workflow vs a stable ~2.1s user-CPU) AND can flatter sui vs nix's warm-cache wall. A cell regresses only if its user-CPU crosses its committed floor; an improvement ratchets the floor down. Wall numbers are advisory context, not the gate.
perf_ratchet_protocol.why: You cannot 'ensure clear performance' on a metric that lies under load. This is the STRATOSPHERE §0 perf-ratchet's measurement foundation.
